text: Silas Alexander Holcomb (August 25, 1858 – April 25, 1920) was a Nebraska lawyer and politician who served as the ninth Governor of Nebraska from 1895 to 1899, running under a fusion ticket between the Populist and Democratic Parties. Born in Gibson County, Indiana, he helped on the family farm and attended local schools during the winter. At seventeen, he began teaching school. After his father's death in 1878, he moved with his mother and siblings to Hamilton County, Nebraska in 1879. He worked at the Thummel & Platt law office in Grand Island and was admitted to the Nebraska bar in 1882. On April 13, 1882, he married Martha Alice Brinson in Mills County, Iowa. They moved to Broken Bow, where he farmed and practiced law. From 1891 to 1894, Holcomb served as a 12th District judge. In 1894, with the support of William Jennings Bryan, he was elected Governor of Nebraska and was re-elected in 1896. During his tenure, sounder financial policies were initiated, corruption and mismanagement in the state treasurer's office were addressed, and reforms in state government programs were begun. Following his time as governor, Holcomb was appointed a judge of the Nebraska Supreme Court in 1899 and served as chief judge from 1904 to 1906. He left the Court in 1906 but later served on the Nebraska Board of Commissioners of State Institutions from 1913 until his failing health required him to resign. In 1896, Holcomb was accused of tampering with ballots concerning constitutional amendments. In 1899, The Norfolk Weekly News accused him of ballot fraud in an attempt to "steal two seats on the supreme bench" during a party meeting, alleging that votes were changed and that when a recount was requested, "Holcomb paid no attention to their suggestions." He was ultimately appointed to serve on the court in 1899. Holcomb moved to Bellingham, Washington, where he lived with his daughter until his death on April 25, 1920. His body was returned to Nebraska, and he is interred at Broken Bow Cemetery, Broken Bow, Custer County, Nebraska.
